gen-gf-gabarito-gf-kadwa: Kadwa has a generous lowercase and curves that stay open at the ends, giving it a classic, editorial voice. Gabarito keeps a constant marker line overhead, and that is the draw.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-piazzolla: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Piazzolla lifts its lowercase nearly to capital height, a notch above the heading's, so the two interlock.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-scope-one: Scope One reads generously, its counters spilling into the surrounding space while the ascenders and descenders stay stubby. And beside Gabarito, whose heading line stays compass-pencil uniform, extended reading feels smooth and unhurried.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-slabo-13px: Bookish in manner, Slabo 13px gives its rounded letters large, clear openings that never feel pinched. What stands out is how Gabarito draws everything with one round pen.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-suwannaphum: Gabarito hums along in a flat, constant line weight, its open terminals letting the counters flow outward. Suwannaphum adds woodblock-high lowercase beneath, so the page gets a firm footing.
gen-gf-gaegu-fs-literata: A marker-like constant line gives Gaegu its casual, inviting hand, with generous chisel-notch openings. And Literata adds sturdy hairlines and slightly heavier strokes, a bookish body suited to bite-sized reading.
gen-gf-gaegu-fs-synonym: Loose, handwritten charm marks Gaegu, with a marker-like line and generous chisel-notch openings. And Synonym, a sans of constant ink, can sit at modest sizes for a few quick lines.
gen-gf-gaegu-outfit: Outfit reads cleanly and approachably, its curves stopping well before they close, like bent cable. And next to Gaegu, with its casual hand, it stays pleasant in modest portions.
gen-gf-gaegu-plus-jakarta-sans: Gaegu writes with a casual, marker-like line and generous openings. It belongs at display sizes, over a few words, while Plus Jakarta Sans, monoline with curve endings kept apart, stays pleasant in measured helpings.
gen-gf-gochi-hand-fs-epilogue: Lowercase that crowds up toward the cap line gives Gochi Hand its hand-drawn, friendly feel. But where Gochi Hand brings personality, Epilogue, a wire-like monoline body, keeps brisk reading smooth.
